intro.title: Hello, I'm Ming
intro.desc:
I am currently pursuing a Master's degree in Applied Data Science at the UVic.

My work and research interests focus on data science, machine learning, and biostatistics. My projects related to large-scale data analysis and applied statistical modeling.

item1.title: PIMS VXML Biostatistics Research Project
item1.desc: Explore and process new statistical methods for zero values in microbiome data, and evaluate popular imputation methods in the mainstream of biology

project1.title: A Novel Statistical Method for Handling Zeros in Microbiome Data
project1.desc:
In this study, I designed and implemented simulation experiments for biological data to systematically evaluate and compare four widely used imputation methods. The evaluation was conducted using a range of statistical and machine learning metrics, including reconstruction error and ecological diversity preservation, to assess the performance of each method under complex biological data settings.

The entire research workflow was built as an end-to-end analysis pipeline using Python and R, incorporating compositional data analysis and phylogenetic distance matrix computation. In addition, I incorporated multiple complex parameters into the biostatistical simulation models to examine their simulation fidelity and computational efficiency, as well as to explore strategies for improving model runtime performance.

event1.title: Supply Chain Business Data Analyst Intern
event1.desc:
Focused on supporting inventory and logistics decision optimization. Designed and automated multi-source ETL data pipelines, integrating Resource Planning, Warehouse Management System, and transportation system data to ensure data consistency and Service Level Agreement compliance.

Built KPI reports and dashboards based on time series forecasting and classification models, reducing inventory holding costs by 18%. Combined Geographic Information System route optimization with replenishment strategy A/B testing to optimize logistics and inventory planning, shortening delivery cycles and reducing transportation costs by 15%.

event2.title: Business Data Analyst Intern
event2.desc:
Implemented a churn prediction pipeline covering over 30,000 customers, addressing class imbalance through down-sampling. Conducted exploratory data analysis, anomaly detection, and feature engineering, significantly improving data completeness and model stability. Performed comparative tuning and optimization, ultimately achieving 85% identification accuracy while maintaining a balance between precision and recall.

Presented the model outputs through Power BI dashboards for business presentation, directly supporting marketing and operations teams in developing targeted retention strategies. Combined with A/B testing, customer churn rate was reduced by 15% within 6 months.

event3.title: Research Assistant
event3.desc:
Researched and analyzed imputation methods for highly sparse biological data. Collected and reviewed various published imputation methods, with a particular focus on exploring modeling approaches that integrate phylogenetic tree-related distance metrics.

Implemented a novel statistical imputation model that introduces biological prior structure into a latent variable modeling framework, significantly improving data reconstruction accuracy, feature interpretability, and effectively enhancing the computational efficiency of the imputation algorithm while maintaining model stability.

event4.title: Data Analyst
event4.desc:
Analyzed the accuracy of resume screening product, with core responsibilities focused on improving resume screening and job matching efficiency through data and algorithms. Lead an end-to-end Resume–Job Matching project, cleaning, standardizing, and performing text feature engineering.

Used Python, SQL, and NLP techniques, built a matching scoring model that improved job ranking precision by approximately 85% and reduced manual screening time.
